findings.claim: The README says the attribute is not emitted for netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, but ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists in netstandard2.0 with .NET Standard 2.0 API surface (System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is available in netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+). The guard likely drops the attribute needlessly, so 'all generated code' is not decorated for those targets and the requirement is only partly met. Also, NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK symbols are defined only for the consuming project's TFM, and the README does not document the exclusion rationale.

receipt_plan.detail: Check docs for ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute applicability: it is in netstandard2.0 (mscorlib/System.Diagnostics). Compile a netstandard2.0 consumer with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to confirm it builds, which would show the #if guard is unnecessary.

findings.claim: The attribute is applied only to top-level generated types (formatters, resolver, nested helper classes). Nesting partial types emitted by EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and other generated pieces, such as the GeneratedMessagePackResolver attribute or the check-in-generated static helpers, are not decorated, so 'all generated code' is read narrowly. This is a scope-interpretation matter.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun snapshot tests and grep the generated outputs for types lacking ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, such as nesting partial types.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional, no setting: add the attribute (guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK) to every generated formatter, resolver, and helper class emitted by the templates, with no opt-out option.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add an opt-out setting (e.g. a property on GeneratedMessagePackResolver or an MSBuild property) so users can disable ExcludeFromCodeCoverage emission, with the templates conditionally writing the attribute based on that option and the default left on.
